extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community: investigators, grant applicants, institutional research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH policy updates, resources, and guidance relevant to preparing and managing NIH grant applications and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select models appropriate to your research question
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions, even as NIH encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential (including New Approach Methodologies - NAMs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease; choose models that best address the study's aims and balance human relevance and translational potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects format
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn key features and application format for NIH’s Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure, including how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview video to understand PF5 structure and submission expectations prior to applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format is available based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare DMS Plans using the specified 2026 pilot format and include the required simplified elements; consult the resource for exact formatting and content expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address replication and reproducibility in applications
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH emphasizes embedding replication and reproducibility throughout research, applications, and awards as part of the Gold Standard Science plan and a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should include considerations, plans, or activities that strengthen reliability (replication/reproducibility) where appropriate and may align with NIH highlighted topics encouraging such efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'Competitive But Not Discussed' scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency review modifications, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed' when falling below a 33% cut-off; strong applications can still receive this designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants receiving 'competitive but not discussed' should understand this category may reflect procedural cutoffs rather than a judgement that the application lacks merit; seek available NIH guidance about next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know centralized peer review at the Center for Scientific Review (CSR)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH consolidated peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR); centralization is intended to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and institutions should be aware of the CSR's role and any implications for review timing, study section assignment, and procedural expectations following consolidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay informed via NIH Extramural Nexus communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscribe to NIH Extramural Nexus emails and use NIH news resources to stay informed about updates, policy changes, and resources affecting the NIH extramural research community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly consult NIH news, guides, and resources (e.g., NIH Data Book updates, policy notices) to ensure application and award practices reflect current NIH requirements.
